text: I really liked this hotel - location is great and the staff are very friendly. I stayed there for three nights when attending a conference in Boston. The rooms are very nice, clean and in a good state of repair. Good selection on the room service menu and not too expensive. From the hotel you have easy access to downtown Boston and a wealth of restaurants and bars to explore. Ask the concierge for tips if you are unsure. The staff are very very helpful and do everything to make your stay enjoyable. Only downside is the entrance - which is a bit weird - and the small gym that does not have daylight.

text: Room is so small that I was initially claustrophobic. Bathroom is about as small as our toilet at home. Double beds should be outlawed! Who can get a good night's sleep in a bed so tiny? Staff are indifferent, although concierge was very helpful. No help offered with our 5 bags, no tea & coffee making facilities in room & no food services on site. Location is ok for walking to Times Square & Empire State Building, but not a good area for decent restaurants. This is not value for money & we would not stay here again.

text: Stayed one night. Looks like every holiday inn express. Friendly staff at check-in. Pillows were poor quality. I did got upgraded to suite which offers lots of space. Got free popcorn at check in. Not a lot to do in the evening.
label: your_label_here

text: My 1st critera for Valentine's Night was a hotel with 2 person jacuzzis in the room. The Drury upgraded us to a really nice suite with a hugh jucuzzi. They had a nice snack/supper at 5:30pm and a tasteful morning breakfast. We walked on the riverwalk at sunset to our resturant for dinner. We will always book this hotel for the Riverwalk.

The pool was clean and nice to relax in the sun while the kids played in the pool. Pool side food service was quick and was not to expensive. They had a limited outdoor menu, but asked for options and you could have whatever you wanted. It did get a little bit noisy being next to the airport, that would be the one downside. Outdoor area had nice world music playing and hot tub as well. Overall great value.
label: your_label_here

text: We just came back from celebrating out 6th wedding anniversary in Philly and could have not stayed in a better hotel! It is actually our 3rd time staying. The room was very clean and all of the staff was cordial. The spa and gym are great and we really enjoyed the sports massages at Breathe, their spa. It is easy to walk to shopping on Chestnut and Market streets and Broad st. We stayed on a club floor and had wonderful views of the city at the breakfast, which had a wonderful diverse selection. We are already planning out next trip to Philly with the kids and we are definitely coming back to Loews!
label: your_label_here

text: My mom and I travelled to San Francisco for the first time on the Labour Day long weekend. We didn't want to have to spend +$250/night on a hotel, so I was thrilled when I came across the Hotel Mayflower. It is a great hotel at a great price! The hotel is old, built in the 1920s, but that just means it has so much character. It's got a great lobby area, and the old style elevators with the gates that pull across. There's a continental breakfast everyday, which has toast, muffins, scones, hard boiled eggs, yogurt, oatmeal, juice, coffee, teas, etc. We were there for 5 days and ate breakfast there everyday without getting bored of it. The rooms are quite spacious, and are all suites, so they have kitchettes which is nice to be able to have drinks and snacks if you like. They've got a little grocery store right next door which is convenient. The staff at the hotel are all quite nice and helpful. It's in a great location! So close to the cable car line, Union Square, good restaurants etc. We would definitely recommend this hotel for anyone going to San Fran, and will for sure go back ourselves.
label: your_label_here

text:
We went to Philadelphia to celebrate our 1 year anniversary and could not have felt more at home than we did at the Morris House. 
First, let me tell you, this is an excellently executed Hotel/B&B hybrid. Built in an old house, you would think there would be some shabbiness and some weird smells - Not true at all!!! The rooms are wonderfully clean with impeccable historic design. I cannot write this review without mentioning our spacious the rooms are. Truly, this hotel felt like home away from home. 
The staff were amazing as well. We arrived very early in the morning (about 6 hours ahead of check-in). They stored our bags and immediately offered us a complimentary breakfast. All three members of the staff we interacted with (Samantha, Lenka and Lowel?) were incredibly knowledgeable about Philadelphia and extremely pleasant. You couldn't ask for better service. 
Here are some pros and cons about the Morris House Hotel
Pros:
+LOCATION! Literally, a two minute walk to Independence Hall. So close to all the historic places that we were able to go back for a quick nap and afternoon tea (really, we just ate the cookies).
+Complimentary Services - breakfast (delicious), afternoon tea (lovely), free wifi (a little spotty, but still great), fully outfitted like a hotel (hair dryer, toiletries) - they even have umbrellas to rent (free but they hold your credit card number in case you don't return it) in the event of unpleasant weather.
+Cozy rooms. Modern heating and cooling make the rooms very comfortable. Tons of storage for items. Comfortable beds.
+Emphasis on safety. The Morris House has taken great care to ensure the safety of their guests and ease any stress. Fabulously done!
Cons: (These were not cons for us, but could be for other people)
-Directly over the Philadelphia Metro. Occasionally, the passing trains underneath would shake the house. Noticeable if you were awake but was not so bad that I woke up during the night (I'm a very light sleeper).
-Holds Events. Hotel hosts many weddings and events. We were on the 3rd floor and couldn't hear a thing, but I'm not sure about the lower floors.
-Room Service is absurdly priced - though it is more of a B&B than hotel, so that makes sense.
For reference, we stayed in room 301.
We would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Philadelphia - though please read the fine print (historic house = no elevator and not best suited for children). You definitely get your moneys worth here. Can't wait to go back!
label: your_label_here

text:
We stayed at the Conrad for two nights. The room was reasonable sized with a very comfortable bed, good bathroom and nice toiletries. I would have liked the ability to make in room coffee as most hotels nowdays include this.
The position of the Conrad is great inner city. Close to everything. The staff are efficient and friendly. Breakfast good with several options both hot and cold served at your table. A nice outside bar area with drinks and snacks.
We had very little sleep the first night as sirens are very audible from the room. We were surprized at the noise and did check - yes there is double glazing so not much can be done about this by the hotel. Perhaps a room elsewhere in the hotel would have less noise. We were positioned on Michigan Avenue.
label: your_label_here

text:

The price was about $35 less per night than Heartbreak Hotel Down the block.
Our Only complaint was of the 3 In house Elvis Movie channels Provided Only 1 of them worked.

text:
Great place for a 3-night stay. Our king room overlooked the pool and was very quiet. But we sure did not need the bed's heavy comforter in the Texas heat. Fortunately, there was a light blanket in the closet. 
Service could not have been better. Staff members were amazingly helpful, friendly, and knowledgable about the area. I made an online reservation the day before I wanted to arrive, and I requested a room without scenting cleaning products and away from the elevator. Staff made sure BOTH requests were fulfilled! Later when the in-room telephone misbehaved, a hotel employee was promptly there to fix it. A front desk clerk knew just where to find a nearby self-serve carwash. When the TV was blaring in the breakfast room, we were able to get the sound turned down. During our visit, we bought a new camera and accidentally trashed the camera box with the strap inside. Our garbage had just been taken out, so we asked if we could check the trash. A staff member volunteered to check the garbage, and he found the box, retrieved the strap, and had it delivered to our room in very little time!
Bonuses included the freshly baked cookies at the front desk and DVDs to check out for free (the rooms have DVD players).
label: your_label_here

text: I stayed at the Fairfield Inn and Suites in San Diego for three nights. The hotel was reasonably priced, centrally located, and the room was clean, and nicely furnished. The microwave and mini-fridge came in handy, while the continental breakfast was much more than I expected. The staff was helpful and willing to print directions to a variety of places. I would highly recommend this hotel.
label: your_label_here

text: The New Yorker is perfect if you want a hotel thats central and close to everything! For starters, we flew into JFK airport and got a taxi to the hotel which is a flat rate of $50 + any tip you decide to give. We was on the 31st floor (thank god for lifts!) The room on first impression was small, but was clean, very modern and comfortable. The bed was also very comfortable. Considering it is the city that never sleeps, we didnt hear much noise outside, even with the window open. You can however hear sirens, and there you will hear a few whilst your there! The maids were very friendly and always smiling!! In terms of food, there is a diner attached to the hotel called the Tick Tock diner. We always ate breakfast there. Good choice at reasonable prices. Sometimes the staff were rude but think this was due to stress because of how busy it used to get. New York as a city is fantastic. The hotel is literally next to Madison Square Gardens, less than 5 minutes to Macys and less than 10 minutes to Empire State building. It is also about a 10 minute walk to Times Square. We went to see Mary Poppins and Sister Act musicals, both were fantastic! Just a bit of advice on attractions. The Hop On Hop Off bus tickets are fantastic. We used the Red Buses (Gray Line). If visiting Statue of Liberty, go early as the queues are sooooo long!! We visited Empire State building in the day, and Top of the Rockerfeller at night - both fantastic!! So, if visiting New York, definitely considor the New Yorker. Perfect city centre hotel!!!
label: your_label_here

text: I know it's pricey, but as they say location is everything and this is right in the middle of where we wanted to be (Times Square), so that helped our trip be even more enjoyable. The cost here is still comparable to prices of other hotels in the area, but I wish they would include WiFi in the guest rooms (especially since AT&T had two towers go down in the area, and my data connection was at zero almost the entire time of my trip). And I wish the hotel had better pillows and mattresses (like TempurPedic), but what they had was pretty standard for most any hotel anywhere and not what I would expect in a luxury hotel. I highly recommend a Times Square view and a high floor. Ours was on the 35th floor and an excellent (if not the best) view, and it was quiet and not noisy at all. I was told our room could go for $1800 on the night of New Years Eve. Our bathroom had a broken tile on the floor, and the water drained slowly out of the bathtub, but otherwise this was a great room. text:

text:
I've stayed at this hotel twice in the past, the latest being four nights during a business trip. The location is good, right near the corner of Market St and Kearny. The business district is an easy 10 minutes walk away. I would consider this hotel "Very Good" if you can get a nightly rate that is $200 or less per night. 
On both occasions that I've been here, the lobby has tended to be quite busy. There's a short wait to check-in. The check-in area has about 5 stations but it never seemed to be fully manned whenever I've stayed here. Usually, there were about 2 reception staff working. After check-in, the elevator banks are right around the corner and they arrive fairly quickly. I've stayed on the higher floors for SPG members. Hallways are bright and clean. I was given a true king bed room. The whole hotel has the non-offensive modern design that tends to be middle of the road. It is neither breaktaking nor repulsive. Same holds true for the room. Let's say it's ho-hum. There's a great amount of space in the typical SPG king bed room, guessing easily above 300 sq ft. The bed was comfortable. The bathroom was of good size. My main complaint is the lighting is poor in the bathtub since there is no overhead or sconce light source near the tub. Standard Westin toiletries are used. The ceilings are very low in the hotel, especially in the rooms. I'd say it's about 8 foot. But the views are exceptional from the rooms.
I did not use the WiFi this past stay, although I do remember it was decent in my previous stay. No experience with the fitness/health club.
The key with this hotel is securing a nightly rate that's not greater than $200 (before taxes). San Francisco hotels tend to have wild fluctuations from week to week due to the high number of conferences/conventions in the city. If you're paying more than $200, I don't think this hotel would be an advantageous deal unless you received a suite upgrade.
label: your_label_here

text: Spotless Garden Inn - meets all expectations. Friendly staff, good breakfast (this one has you order from a menu - breakfast skillet was good and waitstaff recognized that I was in a hurry and got the order out fast). Fitness center is available 24 hours, but the pool is more limited This is new, like the IND airport terminal, and so neighborhood amenities have yet to develop. Therefore, if you don't have a car, you could be stuck. Finally, I did notice airplane traffic, but was not bothered by it. text: A beautiful location for a great three day tour in and around San Diego. The lobby was beautiful with a fireplace, comfortable seating areas and nice views of the bay. We took another couple with us and had rooms on the west end of the second floor with balconies looking out over the harbor. It included free gated parking and breakfasts. The resort personnel were friendly and responsive.(Tina & Andrea) The resort is not new and shows a little wear of time, but it was clean and neat. The maintainance man was at our room within a couple of minutes to fix a small problem. They set us up with a great sightseeing tour of Old Town, Balboa Park, San Diego Zoo, Little Italy, Coronado Island and the Gaslamp Quarter. The breakfasts in the beautiful dining room were very good. The waiters (Francisco and Jesus) were attentive and good. The pool and hot tub were enjoyable after a great day of sightseeing. We will return with other friends.

text:
The Chancellor is an old hotel just off Union Square. If you like:
Tiny rooms (even compared to European rooms)
Bedroom walls with no wallpaper and rough looking walls
A tiny bathroom with no space to put anything
Bathroom tiles and bath which have been painted but are now chipped
A shower with no pressure
Narrow corridors
No aircon
Only two lifts to serve all of the floors and the cleaners
A hotel bar that closes at 9.30pm (sometimes - it was open later on our first night)
Helpful porters
Original features (interpret this as you wish)
Bedrooms where you can hear what's going on next door
Noisy toilet flushes (you can hear next door's as well as those above)
Comfy beds
Clean rooms
Good wifi
A central location

text: My wife and I had stayed at this hotel for a night a few years ago when it was called the Omni and had a nice time, although our visit was very brief. So I was pleasantly surprised when my Hotwire purchase turned out to be the (now named) Roberts Riverwalk. First of all the location, to my taste, is wonderful. Despite the number of abandoned industrial buildings in the area, the River Front is beautiful and there are many parks, concert venues and a surprising number of bars, restaurants and breweries tucked in between the various brooding, empty buildings. I never had any problems and the police are very present. I felt very safe in the neighborhood. For whatever reason I like this type of gritty, urban area. If you prefer something closer to the city night life, or you aren't comfortable in wandering around abandoned buildings, well then you probably wouldn't be in Detroit in the first place. Upon entering you have to walk up a short set of stairs to reach the lobby (unless you notice the ramp that heads down to the bar area and gives access to an elevator before you enter) I had a couple boxes of samples, some dj equipment and my bag so it took me 3-4 trips up and down the stairs to get to the lobby. There was no bellman...The Lobby is very nice, there is no counter, the staff sits at Desks to check you in which is more personal in my opinion. There was a nice fire in the fireplace, Christmas decorations were up and it made quite a nice impression, once I caught my breath from my little stair work out. Once out of the lobby the hotel starts to show its age a little bit, stains on the carpet, some dirt on the walls etc... But I would say it has better decoration and appointments than 75% of the hotels I stay in, just could use some real TLC... My room was nice if a little dated, but had all the amenities I like - Free internet, Free parking, flat screen tv, nice desk, plugs, real glasses instead of plastic etc... The hole punched in my closet door should be fixed, but If this were the end of my stay I'd give the Hotel great if not rave reviews... But.... If you wish to avail yourself of the restaurant or lounge area downstairs this is where the Roberts Riverwalk really needs to step up its game... The continental breakfast that is included with the room, is not continental or breakfast by anyone's standard. A small bowl of fruit, some chunks of pastry on a plate and coffee is not really breakfast. Lunch wasn't better. Since I was working in my room for the morning, I wanted to grab a quick lunch before leaving for my appointments. I went down to the restaurant / bar and pulled up a seat. I didn't see a soul for 15 minutes. I finally called the restaurant from my cell phone and a flustered bartender finally came out from somewhere in the back to pick up the ringing phone, and would have quickly disappeared again if I hadn't called out to him. Lunch was mediocre, a chicken picata that tasted like it had been warmed in a microwave and was so salty I could feel my blood pressure rising as I ate it.... I had originally booked on hotwire for 2 nights, but ended up needing to stay in Detroit an extra 2 nights, so I re-booked using their own website for $35 more per night so I wouldn't have to switch rooms. After a busy day of meetings on my 3rd day, I didn't feel like going out for dinner so decided to give the restaurant another try, big mistake... A surly bartender seemed angry I turned up and disrupted her conversation with another customer (boyfriend?). She disappeared after taking my order and no one came back to fix the skipping CD player for 5 minutes or more. My dinner was as bland as my lunch had been salty and she never asked if I wanted another beer. (same menu at dinner as at lunch)... I retired to my room exhausted after a long day... I was awakened from a sound sleep at 1:15 AM by my room phone ringing... It was the night manager inquiring as to whether I was still in my room or not... Half asleep, I explained that I had extended my stay and confirmed my room with the receptionist in the previous morning. It took her a few minutes to find my new reservation and once she confirmed I had re-booked and paid, she hung up with barely an apology for calling at 1:15... Did this really need to be done at 1;15 AM? I never did fall back to sleep and the more I couldn't get back to sleep the angrier I became... I was willing to overlook some of the blemishes of this hotel, but the rude staff in the restaurant and the middle of the night wake up call has me fuming... Will I try this hotel again? I honestly don't know...
label: your_label_here

text:
My husband and I stayed at the Inn at Penn for a quick weekend getaway. We traveled in late summer, so prices in Philly were still relatively high. We found that this hotel was a good value for the money.
Location: Adjacent to the campuses of UPenn and Drexel. This is a lovely area with many restaurants and bars nearby. It only takes a few minutes to drive into downtown Philly, depending on traffic. We loved this area of the city.
Parking: Hotel offers valet parking, for a price you would expect of a big city. Service was prompt and the attendants were customer focused.
Check-in: Routine check-in. The front desk staff could have been more polished. I remember having to speak to them first during check-in. However the check-in was seamless and since we only stayed one night, this was fine.
Accommodations: The room was nice. Everything seemed clean and the decor was updated. The only downside of our room was the lack of view. I believe we overlooked the roof of the adjacent building. It was cool that the room came with an iPad that allowed you to search the web and order services.
Food: We tried the breakfast buffet on Sunday. It left much to be desired. Its certainly not worth more than $10-$15 at most.
label: your_label_here

text: This is the first time I've stayed at a JW. Have stayed at many Marriotts, and Ritz Carlton hotels. I was very pleasantly surprised at the quality of the hotel, and the service. This resort was the quality of a good Ritz Carlton. As far as amenities, the resort has two 18 hole golf courses, several restaurants, and of course pool and spa. The room was beautiful, large, and clean, as were the resort grounds. Overall, and excellent place for a few days of golf and sun.

text:
This hotel is in a great location. Really near the heart of Boston’s downtown. We stayed in their king suite over the three day weekend. The king suite was roomy, clean, and well maintained.
The nice points of this place:
1. Great Location: It is in the middle of everything. So you can walk to just about anything and the fantastic service! The hotel was only a short walk from the Boston Aquarium and Faneuil Hall, which has a variety of places to eat and shopping. Easy access to the T stop from government center.
2. Quincy market, Boston harbor, and great restaurants are within walking distance. AND it's very quiet in the night despite of its great location!
3. Several pubs and places to eat around within a block of the hotel which is always nice. This was nice since we got in late, and still had plenty of available places to eat after a flight. 
4. The manager went out of his way to help make our stay comfortable.
5. The staff was very friendly and helpful.
6. The rooms were clean.
7. The bed was comfortable, as were the pillows.
8. Breakfast at Nix’s Mate was good and the scrambled eggs with potatoes were nice. However, the breakfast did fill up fast and there were frequent lines and longer waits when we chanced too late. 
9. They have roll away bed available for children. 
The Cons:
1. No swimming pool.
2. No room refrigerator, just a unit that keeps things chilled. 
3. The bathroom grout could have been a bit cleaner.
label: your_label_here

text: I held an event at the SLS Beverly Hills for a client in October and was incredibly pleased with the quality of the hotel and, more importantly, the friendly "customer service" attitude of the hotel staff! I expected a bit of "snobbery" since this was in Beverly Hills but was pleasantly surprised that this was not the case in this hotel. I know it is cliche to say that the staff was able to "think outside the box" but they certainly did in many ways and I would not hesitate one instant to place another event or stay at this property. It was excellent!

text:
Located on 52nd St, you're just blocks from Rockefeller, Times Square, Central Park. Everything's within walking distance. Decent size room, 12th floor. Stayed one night. Didn't use any amenities of the hotel. It's a good choice among lower priced 3-star hotels. We would stay there again for sure. We had tickets to a show at the Beacon Theater on 74th. Decided to walk back to the hotel after, nice mild night. Enjoyed seeing the Lincoln Center all lit up. 
Bathroom shower was STRONG. Nice. We parked a street away and had an online coupon for $30 for 24 hours. Should have cost $50. 
Love New York. Clean, safe, friendly. If only everything wasn't so darn expensive!
label: your_label_here

text:
*Stayed here for a Saturday night on a free night stay from Marriott reward card. The room was newly renovated and clean. This hotel was formerly a Westin and I was told by the staff that Marriott came in and updated the lobby and rooms. Hotel is slow and the city center closed for the most part on the weekend...although the ice rank was open for use. The hotel staff was friendly and eager to please. 
*FYI-The valet parking option is 24.90 with tax. 
*The hotel is in the Arts District of Dallas with many options available for the guests. Our room faced Downtown on the 15th floor and we could hear sirens at one point, although I am sure that is common in a downtown environment.
*The air conditioner did blow on the bed all night which I do not like, but others might enjoy. The a/c did work well on a hot day in Dallas. 
*All said...I enjoyed the stay, loved the clean updated room, and would not hesitate to stay again.
label: your_label_here

text:
i've been here 3 separate times.
front desk staff are courteous.
breakfast is typical of marriott hotels. 
rooms are well designed and decorated with state of the art appliances.
orientation of the buildings (10, i think) is a little confusing, depending on the building you're in. 
internet is very slow and drops during peak hours. 
the bathroom walls are covered in hair and yellow filth of some-kind. 
i've never experienced a shortage of hot water.
fairly quiet but you can hear loud cars from the distant (i-15 no doubt). 
a fair number of restaurants (chipotle, wendys, olive garden), a bar or 2, a grocery store (albertsons), and a golf course are within a miles distance. 
if the rooms were cleaner and the internet was faster i would give this place a 4 or 5.
label: your_label_here

text: I find shopping in that area to be so touristy bourgeois, but we wanted a place under $200 in the city so we could catch the trains and buses to the Shedd and Sears Tower. Mission accomplished, as the 146 bus leaves near there for the museum campus and the Chicago L station is a short five block walk. Nice in that way, but you wind through tons of tourists trying to by happiness at the ridiculously overpriced stores. The suites are quite small. While there is a separate bedroom with un-lockable doors, the living area is tight. The pool is very small for this large of a hotel but offers a really nice view of parts of the city and lake. Parking is 55 bucks a night for valet. We opted for a garage down the street. The location is also nice since it is about 3 blocks from Oak St. Beach on Lake Michigan, which is one of the better areas. We also walked from Navy Pier to the hotel in about 20-25 minutes, so that is a plus. It is a fine hotel for under 200 around there, but the area is so full of shallow consumerism it is sickening.
label: your_label_here

text: We just returned from a wonderful stay. The service was excellent and rooms extremely clean. We loved the location-walking distance to all sites we wished to see. The beds were very comfortable and we slept well after walking miles and enjoying the city. The continental breakfast was a perfect start to the day providing bagels, toast, cereal, yogurt, and fresh fruits. We are looking forward to returning.
label: your_label_here

text: We celebrated our 25th wedding anniversary with a two day stay at the Hotel Monaco in Baltimore, Maryland. Built in 1906 as the headquarters for B&O Railroad, most of the architecture and detail was carefully restored in the Beaux Arts style. The hotel’s lobby area features a spacious lounge with a complimentary afternoon wine hour. Beautifully appointed rooms. Ours was handicapped accessible. Management and staff were very attentive and accommodating. The B&O American Brasserie is available for meals (on the street level).
label: your_label_here

text: Hi fisherman wharf is in a great location. We stayed in the annex, it's quiet and clean. Easy access to roads. The building is older but maintained well. We paid 196 a night. Great price for location. Would recommend, we only slept in the room. Free wifi a plus.
label: your_label_here

text:
I was on business in San Diego and stayed in the W Hotel. Heard great things about this brand.
I was very disappointed in the quality of the room. Ikea furniture, no outlets to plug in cellphones or laptops. I had to move a bed stand to plug in my cell phone. A hotel that brands itself on being hip - missed it on the technology front.
The walls were paper thin and I could conversations and other activities in the room next door.
The room was clean, the bed comfortable and the bathroom and bath products were great!
I love Starwood hotels - now when travelling - I steer clear of the W brand.
label: your_label_here

text: Location is great. Metro is close and neighborhood is nice, with lots of restaurants & businesses. We had a king suite & it had plenty of room for a rollaway in addition to the hideabed. It was also the cleanest hotel of the four we stayed in on our ten day trip. The breakfast and evening hospitality were great, convenient AND saved us a lot of money. The staff was nice, and would hold a dinner plate for you if you were coming in late. However a staff person recommended one of their "drivers" instead of taxis (which were right across the street) for the one day we needed one, and it cost WAY more. Don't do it! Stick with Metro or get a regular taxi.
label: your_label_here

text: My family and I recently stayed at this hotel. It was conveniently located close to downtown and more affordable than the downtown hotels. Would definately stay here again.
label: your_label_here

text:
Neither of us had ever visited Chicago when the need arose to be on the University of Chicago campus for a few days. While the Burnham isn't exactly close to campus, we wanted to be downtown to experience the city, and planned on making the commute back and forth. The hotel was beautifully located for shopping, walking around Millennium Park, visiting the theater district and the Art Institute. Since we were checking in Easter morning, I wanted to have some flowers in the room to mark the holiday. I called a few days before our trip, and the woman at the front desk, though extremely pleasant, directed me to call a florist that the hotel uses to arrange for the flowers myself. Not a big deal, but I was surprised that a Kimpton hotel wouldn’t be used to fulfilling small requests like that in-house. We arrived EARLY (around 10 AM), and even though they had no obligation to let us check in yet, the front desk staff graciously informed us that a room could be made available for us in about 5 minutes (enough time to move the bouquet I had ordered to our room!). We were shown to a beautiful high-floor room (better views and less street noise), just as I had requested through Kimpton’s In-Touch loyalty program, by a very friendly bellhop who also showed us the room’s amenities and unpacked several of our luggage items to the closet. The flowers were there, though the chocolates I had ordered were missing – never found out if that was a mistake with the hotel or the florist, but I wasn’t too worried by it. Meanwhile, the hotel’s restaurant had our name on a wait-list for Easter brunch, and called up to our room to let us know when a table was ready for us (brunch was good, but pricey). The hotel staff was courteous, professional, and went out of their way to make sure that the beginning of our stay was as pleasant as possible.
Don’t let the distance from UChicago dissuade you from staying at the Burnham if you’re in town for the university. It’s located steps from the Blue Line (direct connection in about an hour to O’Hare), and is about a 15-minute ride on the Metra Electric line from the 55-56-57 Street stop in Hyde Park for the university. The $3 ride on the Metra Electic takes longer and requires you to walk a few blocks, but is a big savings over the $20 you’ll pay to get to campus in a cab.
The hotel itself is gorgeous, from the wrought-iron grilles on the elevator banks, to the super-cool film noir-style office doors in the guest room hallways. The hotel was very clean, the feather-beds extremely comfortable, and the C.O. Bigelow bath amenities were a nice touch. As with all Kimptons, stay here for a well-designed, quirky boutique hotel experience with excellent service, but don’t expect the formalities or other big-ticket amenities (pools, spas, huge gyms) that you would see at a five-star property. Be sure to swing by for the free wine hour in the evening, if you have time. And if you’re sad you left your pet at home, ask for a goldfish to keep you company during your stay. We named ours George.
label: your_label_here

text: My daughter and I were able to get away for four (sunny!) playful days in San Francisco and I was so pleased with our hotel choice. Everyone on staff could not have been more helpful or pleasant with every question and request. I felt everyone tried to go beyond simple expectations. Our room, and lovely granite-covered bathroom, was spotless every day--and the location is right in the heart of downtown, so we were able to walk to so many places we visited. I highly recommend this hotel for business or pleasure!
label: your_label_here

text: Just spent 2 nights at this hotel and can't think of a positive thing to say about the place. Dirty carpets, chipped paintwork on the wood and walls, chipped tiles in the shower unit (a positive health hazard in our opinion), scruffy and scratched furniture, our room was depressing to say the least. It might not have been so bad if the bed linen had actually fitted the bed. Won't be returning here.
label: your_label_here

text: Stayed at the Copley Square Hotel for 3 nights in May for a long weekend getaway. Overall, this is a wonderful hotel with a modern boutique feel. Check-in was quick and easy with no hassles. Our room was a Deluxe King, which was a bit of a tight squeeze (I'm guessing the space was under 300 sf), but not a major issue. Most importantly, the bed was comfortable and air conditioning worked perfectly! The bathroom was spacious and clean. Every day, the maids would leave 2 complimentary bottles of water, a nice touch considering most hotels only offer a $5-7 bottle. Also a very nice service is the Wine Down happy hour, where guests can mingle in the lobby bar over a complimentary glass of wine. All in all, this was a wonderful hotel in an awesome location - 5 minute walk to the Prudential Centre, 5 minutes to Newbury Street, 15 minutes to the Public Gardens and the Boston Common, 25 minutes to Fenway. I will be back to this hotel in future, next time in a suite!
label: your_label_here

text:
We stayed for six nights at the Hampton Inn and had an excellent experience.
The staff at the desk was personable, knowledgeable and friendly. The room was small but clean and perfectly laid out.
New York is a pretty noisy place, but by turning on the fan on the air conditioner we were able to drown out street traffic noise and we slept very soundly when were there. The free continental breakfast was a great way to fuel up and start the day (and to save us money). And the free wifi was a great bonus as well.
We've travelled a fair amount to other US cities and have stayed in much "higher end" hotels than this, but the service and the amenities provided by this hotel were second to none.
Again, kudos to the staff at the front desk. They happily answered all our questions, were very friendly and helpful and stored our luggage for a few hours after we checked out while we killed time before our flight.
I would absolutely stay here again and would unequivocally recommend this hotel to others.
Excellent stay!
label: your_label_here

text: Overall, I was very satisfied. I am very serious about my fitness routine in the morning and your fitness facility was very antiquated and lacked variety. My stay was very pleasant, however. Thank you
label: your_label_here

text: Spent two nights here for a wedding in Brooklyn. The staff members were all exceptionally friendly and professional, from the doormen and bellhops to the front-desk and concierge. I was especially grateful that Kevin, a bartender in the Ritz's off-lobby bar, was able to tie my bowtie -- I would have looked pretty foolish otherwise. He made it look perfect. Our room was spacious and comfortable, with a large bathroom and king-size bed that provided some of the best sleep I can remember in a hotel. My only disappointment was that the fitness center did not offer a sauna or steam room.
label: your_label_here

text:
I really liked the staff. Everyone was friendly and eager to help.
Rooms are slightly small but ok for a business trip. The neigborhood is great.
I did not like the fact that there was no pool. Also I was slightly irritated that the rooms had no bar. I could have had a drink late at night as I was jet-lagged.
label: your_label_here

text:
I am so glad I gave this place a try. I usually stay at Hilton properties – in Chicago the Palmer House or the Wit (although I have tried the Hampton Inn around the corner when the town was booked up with conventions). I think I may have found my new home in Chicago. 
As A Hilton Honors Diamond, I was greeted and acknowledged (nice touch that happens too infrequently at other Hilton properties). I was upgraded to a very nice room (1211) which had a great view of the Hancock tower, the water tower and Michigan Ave. up to Oak Street Beach. Really great! The room was squeaky clean a very spacious. The bathroom was huge as was the entry way. I overheard a guy on the elevator say that 1209 (right next door) was his favorite room at the hotel – so I guess I did well. I liked the high tech entertainment system which had nice Bose speakers and all sorts of hook ups for iPod, other aux., laptop, etc. I was glad the remote came with instructions (wasn’t intuitive) and that the maid put the remote back with the instructions each visit.
I used the gym (well outfitted with what looks like brand new equipment). The only downside was that it was in a windowless room on the 11th floor. But it was great to get in, get it done and get out. I liked that they offered cold towels and headphones in addition to the normal water and dry towels.
I ate breakfast at the restaurant twice (very nice service and very accommodating). The HH breakfast voucher was good for two specified full breakfasts (one healthy and one hearty) or $19 credit. I am on a crazy diet and was able to find great stuff to eat , modified to my requests, very easily with very little in the way of “up charge.” I do think that those without the HH voucher will find the breakfast very expensive (oatmeal and fruit plate was $21). I also ate lunch one day on the terrace off the lobby. Over $40 (with tax and tip) for a very small piece of salmon and a side of steamed asparagus (no drink other than water) seems excessive for lunch in the only restaurant at the hotel. . . .) But I have to admit it was good and I was on an expense account.
The few requests that I made were met with enthusiasm and competence – I appreciate that. Checkout was a friendly breeze and I was on my way. The only wrinkle was that I left my Bose noise-cancelling headphones in the room safe. I didn’t realize it until I was on the plane at ORD. A call to the hotel had them promising to call me back with the status. Not 10 minutes later, before they shut the cabin door, they called to say they had it and would send it to me (charged my credit card – not free or anything – which I sort of this a hotel of this stature should do for a top-tier frequent guest . . . . but I digress). 
Overall, I am a very satisfied guest who will be returning.
label: your_label_here

text:
I chose this property as it was near the Queen Mary Hotel, and the rates for the ship hotel were a little over my budget. The Double Tree was situated right on the harbor and the views/atmosphere was impressive. Double Tree has recently renovated the property, and everything was fresh and clean. The beds were comfortable, and I got a good night's sleep which is unusual for me when traveling. The air conditioner system was very quiet and hardly knew it was running. 
The front desk and service staff were very friendly and responsive. I will stay here again if I come back to the area.
label: your_label_here

text:
This is an elegant small hotel with a staff that can't do enough to accommodate every need. It is an Andrew Harper Alliance property and certainly meets those standards of excellence. 
While it is true that there is some street noise, I'm not sure that is not just a given with an inner-city hotel unless you stay in a goliath sized property high above the street. I'm a very light sleeper and still slept fine. 
The location was convenient and the bell staff was kind enough to provide transportation for us to the Botanical Gardens (highly recommended) and to a restaurant that was further than walking distance away. 
We will definitely stay here again and will recommend it to our friends and family.
label: your_label_here

text:
I'm currently staying at the Intercontinental Times Square. The hotel is a nice property. Rooms are well appointed and functional. Service from front desk was good at check in, although there was 1 small point which I was a bit disappointed with. I booked a "Sky View" room however on arrival was told that all the Sky View floors were unavailable due to works on the plumbing. Disappointing but these things happen so I was ok to move to a different floor. The checkin agent then offered to compensate me for the change by throwing in a free breakfast each day, which I didn't feel was the right value. I indicated that I generally don't eat breakfast so that doesn't really help me and was advised that this was what the hotel was offering. I then asked what the difference in rates would be from the Sky View room I had booked and the room I was given. The difference worked out to be $90 per night.
The fact I had to ask for this is disappointing but other than that I'm quite happy with the hotel overall.
label: your_label_here

text: Was in NYC for five days and four nights for my birthday. My first thought when we entered the lobby was it had a contempoary theme to it and it was nice, but we arrived around 10am and our room was not available so we waited in the lobby. The bellsman will hold your bags (they lock them together with other bags in the lobby area) if you want to explore the city while you wait for your room. Our room was on the 8th floor and it was a simple room with a bed, bathroom, small desk and chair. flat screen TV (mounted on the wall) and a small closet. My trip to NYC was not to be spent in our room but to enjoy the city, so it served its purpose for us to take a hot shower and go to sleep. Although the heating/cooling system was a bit outdated (when we entered the room the AC was on so we turned it off and turned on the heat which took a while for the room to get warm) but we were able to open the window in our room when it became too hot ( I thought that was weird I've never been in a hotel room where you can open the window). So if you are looking for a room where you will have lots of space then get ready to pay for the extra space.... the room was big enough I would not compare it to a closet size room maybe the size of a room that you would find in an older model home from the 70's or 80's but like I said it was practical.
label: your_label_here

text: On my trip to San Antonio I had been booked by my company at this hotel and I must admit it was quite a disappointment. I found the hotel was tired, dark and had really poor food. A comment from a friend when I sent a picture of the room to him was spot on: “It looks like a country inn hotel in England in the 70’s”. Where the service was okay the food was terrible (fat & greasy and the breakfast omelette must have gained me 2 pounds + wasn’t finished cooking and the French fries for my burger came out of frost bags), the water in the room you actually had to pay for (new experience for me, and costly at about $4 a bottle), the showerhead was fixed on the wall at about 180cm and I am 195cm so it wasn’t too easy to shower and my bill was wrong when it appeared under the door (this was corrected by the time I checked out though). I don’t know what the price for the competing hotels are but $370 for two nights and one burger with cola and two breakfasts just isn’t worth it when you top it up with being quite a noisy hotel (you can hear people in the halls and when they flush in their room).
label: your_label_here

text: I've stayed here several times and always found it a pleasant experience until now. Last time I stayed at the CP-LAX, I was not a PriorityClub member and yet I was given a fabulous upgrade. This time, as a PC member, I received no consideration other than a coupon for a free beverage (with an expiration date prior to my check-in date) at the exorbitantly-priced restaurant. An unpleasant surprise awaited me when I got to my room: a $2.95 charge for 2 hours of internet (more $$ for additional time, of course) ... what the F ???? Even Best Western doesn't charge for internet.
label: your_label_here

text: The terrific design of the buildings and how everything integrated with the lovely grounds at the beautiful Cedarbrook Lodge were the picture perfect set up for a great relaxing stay! We live close by but wanted to feel a hundred miles away from the daily worries. Wow! The gracious staff and all the services they provided made us feel so comfortable and worry-free! It is so close to everything but at the same time so far away in it's own Shangri-La setting. Fun fun place that is very peaceful and enjoyable. We had a great time. Thanks Cedarbrook!
label: your_label_here

text:
The style of this hotel definitely has a foot up on its competition in Houston, but the hotel could really be so much more. 
The service was a little cold and unhelpful-we were grilled for five minutes upon trying to go to the pool b/c the hotel had not communicated their guest list correctly. Of course, maybe it was b/c I had our 5 yr-old and pool toys-pretty sure I saw the whites of the doorman's eyes when he saw us coming. Needless to say, when we finally "got in", I was expecting a bit more from the pool area-I could have gone to my neighborhood club pool and had a bit more in both design and ambience. Think off-strip vegas hotel with buffet and drink specials.
 The bar, restaurant and lobby are attractive enough. Room service was a C- at best-they didn't get 2/3 orders right, and the food wasn't anything to call home about. The location of the hotel was fantastic for our weekend intentions-museums, restaurants, and retail. I can't be entirely snarky about the hotel--The ZaZa has a good progressive concept. But they started out the new spicy guy at school and quickly seem to have lost their appeal. Step it up!
label: your_label_here

text:
This hotel is filled with Victoriana and Edwardian furnishings and accessories.There is something to explore at every level. Gas fires in the lounge, chandeliers, historical artefacts. It is geared to old world charm and comfort and does it with style.
Tea and coffee are always available in the lounge and an added touch of luxury is the sherry and biscuits in the afternoon.
The breakfast is good and wholesome.
The staff are extraordinarily friendly.
label: your_label_here

text: I have stayed at this hotel many times over twenty years of travel. And every time I have stayed here it has been due to a cancelled fllight or a missed connection. And this past week it was not different. A flight cancellation and missed connection equaled a night at the Hilton O'Hare. This time it included my husband and daughter and with a late arrival we were both tired and hungry. The check-in process was simple and the staff offered small bottles of water while waiting to check in. While the rooms are smaller than a usual Hilton, they are clean and perfectly fine for a one night stay. The restaurant was closed by the time we arrived, but the sports bar was still open. Burgers and chicken wings were perfectly fine. The wine prices were outrageous but the beer was in line. The continental breakfast in the morning was well above average. If you have an early morning flight, or if you are stranded for the night, this is an incredibly convenient hotel, (you never have to walk outside) with great service and good food.
label: your_label_here

text:
Upon check-in I was greeted by a man at the front desk and he could not have been nicer or more helpful. He informed me of everything that I needed to know. 
The room was spacious, clean and comfortable. I liked the fact that I could open the windows and look out. Nice Building. The location was great for my purposes. The bar seemed to always be hopping but I only had time for a quick drink. The waitress was very nice.
label: your_label_here

text: Was a good price for SF, however, was quite a distance from the wharf and downtown (near the zoo), even though there is a muni that leaves from outside the hotel. Rooms were more like a bed and breakfast than a hotel. They were clean, but outdated. The rooms were fairly noisy. Check in was easy and efficient, although, there was no early express check out, which made it slightly difficult. Would be good for a family with a car on a budget. For singles or couples, pay the extra and stay near the wharf.
label: your_label_here

text: This place has it all: Location, service, cleanliness, spacious bedrooms, cozy ambiance and good price! Perfect option for any kind of trip as it is walking distance from Back Bay as well as North End….
label: your_label_here

text: Wonderful historic hotel in downtown Denver. One block from the 16th street mall, close to all the event centers. Great people, kind caring, and on top of things! Wonderful breakfest, and the cookies and milk at night at to die for!!! Saved one for my long drive home, and it made me smile at how nice this hotel is. Give this hotel a chance and you will never stay anywhere else when you go to Denver!!!!
label: your_label_here

text:
After I landed at o'hare airport and started my search for the renaissance, my lessons started. Firstly i looked up the wrong section in tripadvisor for an airport hotel; on hindsight i should have searched in "rosemont, illinois", rather than "chicago, illinois" . After i walked past the hilton in the airport on my way to the blue line on the "L", my regret started. At the L station, the station workers told me to go to P1 instead where they have hotel buses pick us up. You may be wondering why i never called ahead to ask. Well, this is a strange hotel with no phone number on their website. And of course, they never replied my email. I should have seen the red flags. Unfortunately for me again, by the time i saw their number at the bus bay and called them, i just missed the hotel bus and had to wait for another 30mins in the cold. Go to door 2 by the way
This "airport hotel" is a rather far 20min away from o'hare airport and the entrance is a very strange, small and non-descript door. Front desk was thankfully efficient, as it was already 1030pm and i didn't have dinner yet. The rooms are all indeed suites, with a seperate living area, but it's not 5 star or anything. The shower stall is large, but the 2 tvs smaller than Apple mac screens. The sink seems to leak, and there's no bathrobe. Room service was ok
Will try the airport hilton next time
label: your_label_here

text: Their service is great, brand new rooms I was told. My favorite part was the bed. I usually cannot sleep in hotels, but their beds are fabulous. I was visiting friends in La Jolla and their location was perfect for me. My kids enjoyed the pool all day long
label: your_label_here

text:
I had not been to LA or Venice Beach before but I was impressed with the other reviews I had read on here regarding this hotel.
I was in the States for 2 weeks but in La twice during that time. My plan was to check out Venice On The Beach for the first 3 days. I was met by Greg the hotel MD who could not do enough for his residents. From start to finish I was so happy with the great service,the complimentary breakfast each morning, but the biggest plus was the fantastic location. You really can be on the sand in 20 seconds from the glorious ground floor patio. 
My favourite part of the day was just people watching through the transparient walling. The hotel really is in the centre of the entire Venice strip. The upper floors give access to a geat roof terrace witn unbeliievable views of the board walk and bay area. If you stay here you can really pick out the Venice personalities by just staying put. Some evenings I was happy just to hang out at the Hotel and have a beer on the terrace.
The place was clean,safe and had great wifi and an on site PC with printer. Having stayed here the first 3 days I made it my mission to return for the remaining last 3 days of my 2 week trip. All I can say is that I will return here and the sooner the better.
label: your_label_here

text: So, where to start - I always ask for a bathtub as I love a long soak. There is a bathtub but its half size so no chance of a soak. This could easily have been pointed out when booking but wasn't. On arrival, when asking for a full size tub was told it was $200 a day more for room with full size tub. Also, I'm pretty sure we're in a standard/superior room when we booked & paid for a deluxe. Our room & bed are tiny, friends staying here have much larger room & bed & we booked the same. Fortunately, its such a great city so you don't spend too much time in your room. The bed is small but very comfortable, Frette sheets delightful (& robes & Aveda toiletries). Asked for late check out only to be informed that from 12 noon to 6 pm would cost $249! How?? Lastly, the free wine & breakfast are a really nice treat but I have never been to a hotel that has a room service menu that doesn't have any breakfast items on it. Maybe its an NYC thing not to want to have breakfast in your room.... Location wise, the hotel wins, & the staff gave us great bar recommendations. When returning to my room after 5pm yesterday house-keeping hadn't managed to get to my room. Surely not 4 star service, turn-down/house-keeping happened when I was out for dinner but no choccies tonight!! On the other hand, we did recieve a bottle of wine when we mentioned it was our anniversary. As I say very mixed feelings. Can't say I'd reccomend this place...........
label: your_label_here

text: We were traveling with my 3 year old son, who is a dinosaur fanatic, to the Smithsonian museums and stumbled upon this little gem of a hotel. We try to get a room with a separate living space when traveling with him so that his early bedtime is not our early bedtime and the King suite at the Hotel Helix was just the ticket. We got a great deal on the room ($134/night) through my corporate travel agent. It was very conveniently located to all the Downtown DC museums and attractions, super hip without feeling overly swanky, so we weren't terrified that the boy would do lasting damage. We were given tickets for a free continental breakfast for one morning and a $10 "raid the mini bar" voucher. the only drawback was the $40/night parking fee. Even though we could have taken the car out as often as we would like, there was no need to drive. if I had been smarter about it, I would have found a nearby garage for half the price. Free happy hour was a huge plus. Overall a great trip and friendly, fun hotel!!
label: your_label_here

text: Very nice hotel. I stay in Los Angeles often and I will definitely book here again. The amenities are top shelf. Staff is courteous and attentive. I recommend enjoying your happy hour in the courtyard, especially as the sun goes down. Very sublime.
label: your_label_here

text: We loved staying at the Savoy Suites! The room was great! All the employees, from the desk clerks to the housekeepers, were friendly and very helpful! The desk clerks were the best! They always welcomed us back when we returned from being out and about in DC......they offered helpful hints for getting around, etc......and they were lots of fun to talk to! text:
Residence Inn is great hotel chain on the whole. My family always tries to find one when we visit a new US state. There's always comfort, complimentary food, good wifi, a kitchen complete with a tea/coffee service, stove, fridge/freezer, dishwasher & cupboard with dishes. Great if you want to buy groceries & cook your own meals to save money or have a late night snack. 
What made this DC location great was that it was a few blocks away from a lot of the main attractions & great restaurants. The hotel supplied me with a four-paged handout list of all nearby restaurants. An added plus is that this particular Residence Inn is right next to a pharmacy that also sells groceries, so everything you need for your room is a few feet away from your door.
Service was great, everyone who worked there was helpful & mannerly. The glass door of the closet was accidentally shattered when we tried to squeeze a huge suitcase into the closet. The front desk sent a repairman to our room to check it out, he left & returned with a new glass door to install and in 12 minutes it was as if nothing had happened. What was even nicer was the fact that the hotel didn't charge our room for the accident.
I definitely recommend this hotel, especially if you are traveling with family or friends. Just know that they charge (as of April 2012) $29 a night for parking AND that there's a height restriction because the parking lot is underground. Unfortunately, the huge jeep that we rented was too tall to fit into the RI lot, so we had to park up the road in another hotel's parking lot for $32/night. 
If you can help it, save the cash & don't rent a car at all - regardless of which you hotel you stay in, unless you plan on exploring in your car outside of DC into the wider DMV area. Between the rental fee & insurance and parking fees both at the hotel and around the main streets & major spots in downtown DC, it adds up. Walking is healthier anyway. lol

text: Let me start with the positives, although there were only a few. The location for the Sheraton is pretty much the best part of this hotel. Now onto the bad stuff. I came to check in and they did not have my reservation. Even though I had my confirmation number and copy of my reservation sheet. There happened to be a sorority convention staying at the hotel, but to not be able to accommodate because of high volume of guests is completely subpar for a large hotel chain. After asking to speak with a manager as the clerks told me I didn't have a room, I was finally cleared to check in. The room was pre-paid and the hotel ended up charging me twice for the one night stay and have still yet to rectify my bill. The hotel is pretty expansive, but the decor needs serious updating and the elevators are extremely sketchy. There were a few times I thought I'd be spending hours in them getting up and down the tower. The rooms are of good size, but the windows make you feel like you're staying in a post-Soviet building as they are tiny concrete slits, at least in the tower portion. Best bed I've slept in though, which was somewhat redeeming. I'm more dissatisfied with the customer service of this hotel than anything else, and for this reason alone I would recommend staying far away from this place and booking elsewhere.

Some parts of the hotel room looked a little bit outdated, but were offset by the overall experience.
The biggest issue I found was with the bathroom. There seemed to be an issue with the window seal, as the bathroom was always cold even when the heat was on. This made it uncomfortable in the morning. The windows in the room open, but only a few inches given that there are no screens. Noise can be a problem with people, music and other noise.
The internet was quick, and was free for me. However depending on your rate and room, it will cost you money. There is plenty of storage space with a large closet as you enter the room and drawers for clothes and other items. There is a nice bar next to the lobby. I didn't eat at the restaurant so do not know if it was any good. You can also leave your luggage in storage as you are out on the town after you check out at no additional cost.
I would definitely recommend the Mayflower if you are looking for a place to stay in downtown DC.

text:
This is my favorite hotel in Chicago, and I've stayed at all the top luxury properties (Four Seasons, Hyatts etc). I've stayed at this hotel 20+ times, it's a hidden gem. Right on the lakefront, there's a beach across the street from the hotel, and if you get a lake view room (be sure to ask), you'll spend some quality zen time gazing at the water. Regardless of which room you get, you can leave your window shades open because you have beautiful views in every direction plus no one overlooking you. 
Rooms are fantastic - I love the clever, well-designed furniture and fittings, simple, minimal, and very well-designed. Honey-colored lighting plus a multiplicity of window treatments (blackout shades plus twig shades plus sheer sun shades) means that you can adjust the lighting to make yourself feel cheerful and relaxed. The bathroom is gorgeous, plus clever 'window' out to main room means excellent ventilation and light. 
The huge lobby is my favorite hangout in Chicago. The ground-floor location means you're connected to the street-level location and yet the plush chairs, sofas etc mean that you totally zen out and relax. I always try to conduct business meetings in the lobby - plenty of space, beautiful room and excellent food/drinks menu and service means that my guest invariably remarks 'wow, this is a great place, I've never been here before.' I've won almost every negotiation conducted in the lobby, ply your opponents with drinks plus finger food plus a terry cloth robe and they will give you all that you want :)
Also love the staff - they totally deal with whatever questions I have or help that I need. This is an EXCELLENT hotel for BUSINESS travelers, the staff is exceptionally helpful running meetings, handling phone calls etc. And special shout-out to the car valet staff and doorman staff - Chicago can be incredibly cold, but the staff always has your car (or taxi) warmed up and waiting for you, I've never met better service. Ever. The front desk also have my airplane boarding passes printed out when I come down to check out, plus a pre-visit call means they will help you maximize spg points etc.
Stay here every time you visit Chicago.
label: your_label_here

text: I recently stayed at the Westin Copley in Boston, MA while visiting family for Thanksgiving. I stayed in a Junior Suite (Room 1001). Things got off to a negative start at check-in as when I made my reservation, I was told I would have a room on a high floor. The 10th floor is not a high floor, in my opinion. Upon entering the room, I was definitely impressed with the size of the room and the view, despite not being higher up. Let me start with the good before I finish with the bad. The view was spectacular, the room was neat, and it may have had the most comfortable bed that I have ever slept on. Also, the staff was very friendly. Unfortunately, I have more bad comments. The desk in the room was so wobbly that it was un-useable. The bathroom is tiny, outdated, and I find it hard to believe that a hotel charging this much a night still has a shower/tub combo with a shower curtain. It did have a nice shower head but it was useless since the water pressure was so weak. The door in the bathroom is worn, weathered , and generally not in great shape. I had an issue with the TV reception the entire stay. I arrived on a Wednesday and noticed it but did not notify the front desk. Thursday morning it was so bad that I couldn't even watch it so I called the service number. A gentleman came up , did a few things behind the tv and said he had to reset the satellite. The reception never got any better. The noise wasn't a problem here but it is a tad annoying that the doors slam when closing, so you hear that in the hall. I expect that at an economy hotel when I travel on business but did not expect that here. One other troubling note was that there is no security with regards to the elevators to the guest rooms. Anyone can walk in and go to any floor without a room key. One final issue was the morning of check out , it took forever to get a guest services rep on the phone to answer a question that I had. I don't think all of these negatives are a big deal , individually, but add them all up over a 3 day/2 night stay and it impacts your overall experience. Add in the hefty rates, and I would say that the experience was average at best. I am not likely to recommend this hotel to anyone unless they had a super-cheap deal.
label: your_label_here

text:

You can't beat the location and if you've got a little extra to spend then I highly recommend getting a room with a view and on the 6th floor. The 6th floor has balconies, so you can order room service and have breakfast outside looking at the beach. There is a rennovation taking place, but it didn't disrupt my stay. Asdies from some scaffolding outside, I didn't notice it. 
There aren't many restaurants off the boardwalk in Venice, so make sure you make a reservation at High (rooftop bar) or the . It has panorama views of the beach and good food/drink. text:
This was our third stay at The Rittenhouse -- and the first with our teenage daughter. We purchased the Van Gogh Up Close package and were placed in a large (600 sq ft?), quiet deluxe room on the eighth floor. While the layout was a bit odd/awkward, the room was comfortable and well appointed.

We also love having breakfast at Lacroix at the Rittenhouse. Unfortunately, the kitchen was shorthanded the Saturday we were there, which we would have appreciated knowing before we ordered our French toast and omelet, and it took over an hour to get our food (after a delay in getting a server and then our coffee). However, much to the hotel's credit -- and why we will continue to return to the Rittenhouse -- when we told the manager about the problem, he insisted on crediting us the cost of breakfast. 
While the Rittenhouse is not inexpensive (and the various taxes and fees don't help), you are paying for a world-class experience and a great location.

text:
Once again.....reading past reviews of this property gave us a "mixed bag" feeling, but the best way to find out is go there yourself. You like it, you may come back....you don;t like it, you won't stay there again. It's not rocket science, ya know ???
My husband Bill & I spent 3 nights at this property and we would definitely stay here again.
The staff was very pleasant. The food at the breakfast buffet was more than adequate.
The Studio Suite had more than enough room for 2 people. The view was what you made of it.....ours was of the hotel across the street. No biggie.
The ambience and atmosphere of the property was awesome !!!! It's actually a former bank. Speaking of which....you MUST see "the Vault".
The small bar at the back end of the hotel was great as well. Nice spot for a quiet drink. HI MARIO !!!!! He's the best bartender they have. 
Also...one of the best things about this property is it's proximity to the Inner Harbor.....literally an 8 minute walk...indeed....2 blocks. Yes, some of the reviews say that it's not in the best "location". My advice to that......KNOW YOUR SURROUNDINGS.....EVERY BIG CITY HAS THEIR SHARE OF "SAFE" AND "NOT-SO-SAFE" AREAS TO WALK IN AT NIGHT....ASK THE STAFF...THEY WILL BE MORE THAN HAPPY TO TELL YOU WHERE TO GO AND WHERE NOT TO GO !!!!.
As I said at the start of this.....we would definitely return to this hotel again....perhaps next year when the Orioles play the "Sox" at awesome Camden Yards.

KMc-Anderson

text: Our daughter moved to Boston two years ago and lives right down the street from this hotel. On the down side, we have now stayed twice on the ground floor and the door doesn't latch closed without really slamming it. This has happened in two different rooms. Despite coming in late to find this, the young lady at the desk was polite and relocated us right away. On the whole, the Terrace Inn is convenient, clean, budget-friendly, and staffed with friendly people. We'll be there again soon.

text: Arriving by train from CT and finding this Hotel was just across the street from Grand Central was a bonus. When we checked in at 11am and was given our room key was another bonus! Considering how busy the City and Hotel was we experienced very good customer service, especially from the concierge young lady who went out of her way to help us so we would make our train connection. Would come back time and time again for this Hotel and it's location.
label: your_label_here

text:
The hotel was over booked on my arrival date, and we were forsed to stay in a room with 2 double beds rather than the King that had been requested....We were able to move the next day as long as we would accept a room on a smoking floor. Not a perfect situation, but definitely not a reason I wouldn't come back again. Thanks very much to the staff for finding a solution to the problem. 
The hotel was clean (by my standards) but little things were always missing from the room after being cleaned. For example one day no towels, one day no coffe cups etc. 
The hotel is very close to Little Italy, but not much else going on in the neigborhoods around the place. Good Value, but not sure I would book here again??
label: your_label_here

text: Before staying at the Catamaran, I did tons of online research. I probably read every review out there, at least twice. So, we went in not only expecting some of the negatives we read about, but actually looking for them. We did NOT find a single one! What we found was a beautiful little slice of paradise. When we pulled into the circular driveway and were greeted by the valet, I begin to feel a shimmer of hope that this was going to be a great stay. The lobby was beautiful, complete with a waterfall full of koi fish. The grounds were immaculate and lush, and just so beautiful and serene to wander through. We had a studio room on the fourth floor facing the bay. The room was huge with a little kitchenette, sleeper sofa, two beds, and a large balcony with a BEAUTIFUL view. We would sit out on the balcony watching the sail boats go by, while baby ducks wandered around on the grounds beneath us and hummingbirds hoovered around in front of us. It was so nice and relaxing!! The pool and hot tube were huge, with food and beverage service poolside and a FREE arcade for the kids! Then there were the colorful parrots that would say hello to you and were very entertaining. Did I mention this resort is ON the bay? We could walk right out of the hotel directly onto the boardwalk, where they rented all sorts of water equipment. We also loved the Bahia Belle boat ride, which was also free. After the boat ride, we came back to the hotel to find hula dancers and all the tiki torches being lit around the hotel. It was so cool! Our children, ages 11 and 2, absolutely loved this place. I almost forgot, we could see Seaworld and the fireworks from our balcony each night. We did purchase passes to Seaworld (we live in Orange County), and I would honestly probably have traded them in for more time at this beautiful resort. It was an absolutely amazing stay and I know you will enjoy every minute of it, we sure did!!!
label: your_label_here

text:
Perhaps we have been spoilt as having always stayed in Grand Hyatts, primarily on Far East holidays, our expectations were very high, only to be rather disappointed. The stay was perfectly adequate - we stayed 6 nights.
The plus points: convenient location off Union Square, rooms had nice decor, beds very comfortable, top floor restaurant has fabulous views and food was fine. 
The negatives: lobby is dull and front desk check-in experience was disappointing - served by a gentleman (rather unfriendly)... I asked if we could have a higher floor with a view if possible - he replied yes, nice room and good view. We ended up on the 12th floor with no view onto the back of a couple of buildings and some industrial centre roof. Woken at 4am each morning to some form of lorries unloading which we assumed took place underneath the industrial roof we could see below us - this only lasted about 30 mins each morning.
Whilst in-room cleaning was fine with friendly, pleasant maids, glasses/trays were left outside various rooms on the 12th floor and we were astonished to see a couple of particular trays left for 3 days whilst we stayed which had food on! Very poor for this type of establishment.
Grand view restaurant where we had the breakfast buffet each morning had beautiful views - staff were generally very pleasant and accommodating. Food was generally of a good standard, albeit, the hot buffet items did tend to be on the "lukewarm" side, so by the time back to your table, items often cold. Furniture items in bar/lounge area adjacent to restaurant were generally very tired and could do with a facelift.
Check-out : front desk tried to charge us for 6 nights accommodation (which had already been pre-paid through Virgin holidays) - this was quickly rectified once I complained.
Hence, our average rating ... admittedly, we did not complain to anyone about any of the issues we encountered ... provided our room was clean with comfortable beds, we were often not in the hotel long enough to worry about things as we were out enjoying the fantastic city of San Francisco.
label: your_label_here

text: The location was awesome. It was located just down the street from restaurants, clubs, & upscale bowling alley. Close enough to walk. That's where the awesomeness ended. We had to pay to park, which is understandable but $15 per day and not directly in middle of the action. They could cut the guests a break. The hotel was clean but the caulking in the tub was broken and black. The room was not updated and did not feel modern and bright. For a Crown Plaza I expected so much more. Note: The staff was very friendly. They do cater to pilots and flight attendants so you may be pushed aside at the check-in desk.
label: your_label_here

text: Needed a hotel in the Flatiron district that was near a work event and scored a great rate via Hotwire at the last minute. Very skeptical at first because it seemed too good to be true...but pleasantly surprised when it turned out to be a decent place. Beds very comfortable, bathroom clean and modern (but TINY), friendly staff. Only two gripes - carpet had seen better days (a little frayed and stained in places) and if you go to bed early (before 1 am) the live music from the club in the lobby will likely keep you awake. But if you're determined to make the most of your stay in NYC and just need a place to crash late at night, this is definitely a hotel you'll want to consider.
label: your_label_here

text: I have just stayed at this hotel - nice enough but far from special. The worst thing is no car parking, and the guy on reception was not the most helpful in finding me somewhere. The lift was too small and difficult to use for the one luggage cart. I couldn't find any breakfast. Then the bill. I was charged $3 for the internet - you will be charged if you use or not. The final insult was when I asked if we could stay in the room for an extra hour before leaving for the airport. $50 for an hour! I felt that I was being treated like dirt. There are a lot of hotels out there, and I would avoid this one like the plague. The real bonus were the down-and-outs who live outside the front. They were great people to talk to, and it was fascinating to see them all gather when the free food and clothes hand-outs arrived. Great people. Sad for the girl who got beaten up the night of our stay. The Police sorted it out pretty quickly! Finally - the roof terrace (advertised). Great view, nothing up there but a few tatty chairs.
label: your_label_here

text:
The entire lobby and breakfast area is being remodeled. Carpet has been pulled up, walls & furnishings updated, and the breakfast area is in a temporary room with food set up on folding tables. No hot food other than microwaved sausage, egg, & cheese biscuits. Staff was friendly. Avoid the end rooms, as ours was 435 and had a VERY small 'closet' and very small desk. Bath counter was small also. The beds were great, and the room was very clean, though. Our maid left cute and ingenious towel art on our bed each morning (see photo), which earned a tip.
If we could have had a normal room with a normal closet, and they were done with the remodeling, it would probably be a great place.

text: We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn during a long weekend trip to visit the sites. We were 3 adults and one child. The hotel decor was bright, the towels and linens crisp and new, it felt as though the hotel was brand new. Enjoyed being close to the metro although it was easier and cheaper to take taxis. Not sure the surrounding neighborhood would be safe to walk through at night, but the area just around the hotel is fine. Also, you need your card key to use the elevator which made us feel secure. There is a large supermarket on the corner which was great for picking up snacks and toiletries. The pool was very small so don't go for that. The restaurant was pretty good but expensive. The hotel is easy to get to from the Beltway which was nice since everyone told us we'd get lost driving into DC. Would definitely stay there again.
label: your_label_here

text:
a spur of the the minute decision to go Chicago and no hesitation booking this hotel.. Could only get a suite at such short notice but the views form the 5th floor windows on both sides were worth it-views down to the Lake and down the theatre district. The attention every time you walk in is so personal-love the happy hour for wine and one night we missed it so w e were given a free drink at the bar. The bed was the most comfortable ever.
love that a very nice restaurant is on the premises too.
 It's also central to many sights.
The only thing I don't like is the dog policy whilst the ones there were no trouble i find it strange that dogs are allowed in a hotel

text: The Omni is a beautiful and historic hotel located in the perfect location. Guests can walk to Faneuil Hall/Quincy Market, the Common/Gardens, and the waterfront-really can't get much better than that. There is a grand, historic feel to the hotel the minute one walks into the lobby and the staff is fantastic.
