text:
The location was very convenient and while the staff were friendly, they insisted that we use the electronic check in option instead of helping us themselves. Why pay staff if they are just going to direct you to the auto check in??? Which, funnily enough, wasn't working properly and they had to check us in themselves. 
We got home from dinner about 10:30 and proceeded to hear our neighbors have sex. To be fair to them, they weren't being that loud, its just that the walls were paper thin. Awkward. Despite being on the 9th floor and facing an alley, we could hear everything on the street below. I mean I could hear the conversations of the people as they left the bar at 2:30 a.m. and randomly at 5 a.m. there was a crazy person screaming at the top of their lungs for about 5 mins. Granted, its not the hotels fault that there are crazy people on the street or that drunk people tend to be obnoxiously loud. What the hotel could use is some double glazing as I don't think its too much to not hear the street noise from 10 stories up.

text: What a pleasant surprise to a priceline booking. Great hotel, location, staff, etc. We didn't get to try the Mercat restaurant, but the little cafe on the lower level had great drinks and outdoor seating. Definitely recommend and will be returning next time we are in Chicago.

text: Briefly, the service lacked in courtesy and efficiency. When we needed to get new rooms keys because ours stopping working, the desk clerk was curt, as if we were bothering her. text:

The general aspect of the hotel is not so pleasant. It looks old, but not in a good way. Some of the members of the personnel are quite nice, but others showed little interest in being helpful.

text: As always, we had a wonderful visit and stay. Did not take advantage of the cookies at night and the reception was unavailable due to a private party. No worries though. The room ws very nice but could use better lighting. The staff was very friendly and helpful and the free shuttle was another great convenience. Can't wait for our next visit.

text: The outward appearance of the Sheraton makes it look older. That is not the case! The remodel has made the hotel very clean and modern. It is now smoke-free. The pool is clean, and the hot tub is fairly large. The parking garage is under construction, so we could not walk inside to certain parts of the mall. It is highly worth it to get the club room that gives you access to a lounge that serves breakfast in the morning. This hotel has a great location and is very clean. I highly recommend it.

text:

text: I recently stayed at the Millennium Broadway in NYC with my husband, 14 and 11 year old daughters, sister and 18 and 15 year old nieces. It was our first time in New York City and we had preconceived notions of how people would treat us and the service we would get but we were surprised and pleased to learn that we were wrong! From the moment we pulled up to the hotel, the valet parking attendant and the front desk staff were very helpful and friendly. The hotel was clean and suited our purpose for the one night we were staying there. We booked on Priceline and got a good price but we were disappointed when we were informed that they could not give us a room with 2 beds for our family of four because they were fully booked. They did give us the option of renting a cot for $35/night, which just increased our Priceline price but we had no choice. We wondered if they really were fully booked or not. Our room was not ready when we got there but they held our luggage while we went out to explore NYC. We were just a minute walk from Times Square and a short walk to a subway station and the PATH train, which we took to Hoboken New Jersey to Carlo's Bakery. It only took us 12 minutes to get there then it was just a short walk to the bakery from the train station. There are a lot of places to shop and eat near the hotel and there is even a little deli across the street from it where you can buy snacks and drinks till late at night. The room was small and looked like it needed to be updated but if you aren't looking for anything too fancy then I would recommend this hotel.
label: your_label_here

text: Wish I had more time to enjoy the amenities. I like that they have free parking if you park further away from the hotel. A big, big plus. This will be my hotel whenever I am in Houston. The staff at the hotel were all very helpfull. Really nice hotel. Loved the outdoor pool area. But never had a chance to enjoy it as very short weekend trip.

text:
Excellent lcation near Union Square, Westfield shopping mall , cable car and the BART. This is however not really suitable for leisure travel as they are very business orientated. Very impersonal. Massive lobby that is buzzing 24/7 with all sorts. The reception is undermanned all the time and therefore whether you want to exchange traveller's cheques, check-in or out, buy stamps or whatever, there is always a queue. We got allocated a double room with king beds for 4 people and had to move to a one with queen beds after the first night as the original room was tiny ; no room for suitcases anywhere. The room with queen beds was plenty big enough. There was no fridge in the room which ws disappointing.
Breakfast is very expensive but plenty of diners nearby that are much cheaper.
Drop off and pick up fro Alamo rent a car within a short walk hich was a real bonus.
label: your_label_here

text:
We booked this hotel after a recommendation in the Telegraph. Looking at the hotel's website it looks very swishy. The reception is very nice, but your heart sinks when you get to the corridors outside the bedrooms. Artexing gone mad and very basic, but the rooms themselves, although small are adequate and much nicer than the corridors lead you to believe. 
All the staff are very good, especially the "greeters" who always welcome you back and are helpful and have a cheerful word. The standard of cleaning of the rooms we found to be very good.
We booked bed and breakfast, but watch out as this only covers you for a continental and you have to pay extra for cooked. Having said that there is a very nice fresh fruit salad served, nice juice and good pastries and bagels so you won't starve!
We stayed here twice - we had 4 nights first off in a bigger deluxe room which was nice with oblique view of Washington Square. The hotel then agreed to store two large suitcases for us when we travelled outside New York for a week. We returned for 2 more nights in a smaller room, which overlooked an internal courtyard, but this was OK. There are 2 ipads in reception that you can use to find things out. 
The best bit about this hotel, however, is the position. Close to the University and all the restaurants and bars of Greenwich Village. We walked our socks off from here and found it very well positioned for exploring the big apple.
We do hope they are OK following hurricane Sandy I'm sure the great staff will be working their magic again as soon as they can.
label: your_label_here

text: Used marriot points for the room, which was top notch. Great location at Cherry Creek shopping center, a lot to do in small area and is nice place for a stroll. A lot of dining locations within walking distance. Excercise room was very nice, and resturant serves a great breakfast. Bar was hopping even later in pm, staff very friendly, and we were able to get a ride in limo to Coors Field for ball game.

text:
This is a well managed establishment. Staff very friendly and efficient at check-in. Problem with my desk lamp was fixed 3o minutes after calling in the problem and someone called to follow up with me to make sure all was well. Laundry promptly picked up after I called.
Rooms are clean, spacious and quiet even though near main throughfare. Very limited movie choice compared to other hotels. Strong internet WIFI signal. 
On a Monday night at 9 PM, they had closed their signature sefood and steak main dining room because "it was slow" and patrons had to eat in the bar instead which I felt was a bit strange. Service from the bar was quick and friendly though.
Gym is well equipped with TV screens on most machines. 
Decor in rooms and common areas a bit pretentious and stuffy for my taste so I probbaly won't be back, but that is a subjective matter.
I spent three nights here and have no complaints.
label: your_label_here

text:
This is the most expensive hotel I have ever stayed in my entire life but it rates near the bottom in terms of quality. If I had paid the $450 per night the Grand Hyatt charged out of my own pocket I would have checked out after the first night. However, I was tagging along with my wife while she was on business in DC so I only have to wonder why a hotel could charge so much money for a basic room. No this was not a suite, it was a room withtwo double beds.
First the good. When you walk in, the lobby truly looks grand. But this is DC and this is the kind of hotel people stay in when somebody else pays the bill. The breakfast, while expensive ($21 for the buffet) was good. I especially liked the omelets. Service was friendly. We had drinks at The Cure a very relaxing bar. While expensive ($20 for a glass of merlot and a draft beer) the bartender was friendly and efficient. The check in was quick ut when we inquired about the price of wi-fi access the clerk did not know. I decided to live without e-mail for a few days since I was on vacation. What else is good? The location. My wife was able to walk to her meetings offsite and I was able to get to all the tourist hotspots in about 15 minutes.
Now the mediocre. While the lobby was great, we did not sleep there. We slept in what was essentialy a $100 a night room. The beds were comfortable enough and the TV was big, but everything else was rather underwhelming. The bathroom was dimly lit, there was no exhaust fan that we could find, and the toilet seat was broken. The towels looked like somebody bought the cheap ones at a Wal-Mart. The AC unit was on its last legs. We called maintenance to have them look at. They determined it was working OK, and despite it only being about 60 outside, we "just had to turn it all the way down and leave th blower on high". I pity the poor blokes who stay in 247 in July. Apparently the maid's vacuum didn't work either because the floor didn't appear to be vac'd during our stay.
So all in all, a rather unimpressive hotel. I was expecting much more.
label: your_label_here

text:
